scope: Proposition 17.1 (Universal comparison of internal norms) of the manuscript “Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps” (preprints/Metric-measure-limits-of-subcritical-FK-and-spanning-tree-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1dd659698d3a3fde), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 203. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are constants 0 < α ≤ β < ∞, depending only on the fixed Brownian and metric units and on k, with the following property. For every rigid certificate law satisfying (17.2), and every fixed integer i, its internal endpoint norm satisfies αC2−ip ≤ qi ≤ βC2−ip . (17.3) Negative i mean a finite enlargement of the time interval. The assertion applies also to laws obtained by joint extraction of zooms of already limiting laws. Consequently, if q0 = 1, then C− := β−1 ≤ C ≤ α−1 =: C+. (17.4)
